meaning: Identifier of one claim in a draft
used_by_rule: all

meaning: The claim as written
used_by_rule: reviewer reads it

meaning: The confidence the draft states for the claim and its main uncertainty
used_by_rule: Shown to the releaser beside the claim and kept with the released claim

type: entity list with source list and time interval
meaning: Named entities the claim concerns, each with its tenant and identifier namespace, and the sources and event interval the claim covers
used_by_rule: Materiality tiers and full checks of claims about named entities read the entities here; an absence claim passes only if its cited runs' evaluated entities, sources and intervals together cover this scope (query_run_ids); the current-conduct test compares this interval with the task's current period

meaning: True if the claim being false would change a recommendation, a detection candidate or a released statement about named entities
used_by_rule: every material claim must cite records

meaning: True if the claim concerns conduct in the current period stated in the task scope
used_by_rule: a claim about current conduct must cite at least one source observation, normalized observation or derived feature whose event interval lies in the current period; a model or risk output or a control outcome alone does not satisfy the rule; a derived feature that carries an agent-output or released-item link satisfies it only if the claim also cites, for each named entity, a current-period observation among that feature's inputs

meaning: Identifiers of the records cited for the claim
used_by_rule: citation required

required: yes for material claims (may be empty)
meaning: Identifiers of retrieved records that count against the claim, listed by the agent and extended by quality review
used_by_rule: Shown to the releaser beside the claim. An empty list records that none was listed, not that none exists.

required: written by the checker for material claims (may be empty)
meaning: Identifiers of records that the case's query runs returned within the claim's scope but that the draft neither cites nor lists in contradicting_record_ids, each marked by whether the checker's fixed rule classes it as able to count against the claim, such as a report, a reversal or a record of a benign explanation the claim must exclude. The checker writes this field from the query coverage records and records that rule's version; the agent cannot write it.
used_by_rule: Records the fixed rule marks are shown to reviewers and the releaser beside the claim, and the rest are summarized by type and count; full checks of claims about named entities examine every marked record and a recorded random sample of the rest, whose size is fixed in advance for each claim type

meaning: Record class of each cited record: source observation, normalized observation, derived feature, model or risk output, control outcome, analytical inference or finished intelligence. External knowledge is identified separately, with its source and type: observation, assessment or catalog.
used_by_rule: The checker obtains the class and external source type from the cited record. Analytical inferences and finished intelligence may be cited only as context.

meaning: When the cited event happened, with source, trust status and uncertainty; outcome windows use the channel's declared clock-start event.
used_by_rule: Current-period test uses the supported event interval; an unresolved interval cannot pass solely because the report arrived recently.

meaning: When the cited fact first became available to queries. A derived result uses its own availability time, no earlier than any input; input freshness remains separate.
used_by_rule: as-of rule: a cited fact must be known by draft_time

meaning: When this draft version was created; the same for every claim in the version
used_by_rule: as-of rule: each cited learned_time must be no later than draft_time

meaning: Root observations reached by following each cited record's lineage
used_by_rule: Deduplicate repeated records of one observation. Distinct roots do not by themselves establish independence; review known shared sources and common causes.

required: if copied untrusted ledger content or agent output
meaning: Class of copied untrusted ledger content and agent outputs: copied untrusted content; agent output exposed to untrusted content, including evidence-plane content; or agent output without that exposure. Ordinary underlying source observations are not assigned an agent-output category. Exposure takes precedence and survives storage and normalization.
used_by_rule: Ledger copies and agent outputs cannot substitute for underlying evidence-plane records. Other cited records retain source trust and untrusted-content marks and remain subject to their record-class limits.

meaning: Plane of each cited record: evidence, threat knowledge or organizational memory
used_by_rule: agent-proposed inferences may be cited only as marked context

meaning: Identifiers of all recorded agent-output dependencies for each cited record, such as a label, control outcome, detection, derived feature or inference. Section 4.2 governs automatic attachment and authorized removal.
used_by_rule: dependent records are never counted as independent corroboration

meaning: Released item ID and version, with its release decision ID, for each organizational-memory item recorded as informing each cited record, such as a label, control outcome, assessment, detection, derived feature or inference. Section 4.2 governs automatic attachment and authorized removal.
used_by_rule: A record informed by a released item counts as dependent on that item and on any agent output behind it, never as independent corroboration

meaning: True if the claim states that something is absent, did not occur or was not observed
used_by_rule: an absence claim must cite query_run_ids; any claim with unreported_outcome true must also cite channel_state_ids

meaning: True if the claim states or relies on an outcome that was not reported, such as a rate that counts transactions without reports as negatives
used_by_rule: a claim marked true must cite channel_state_ids, and any negative it reads from them is provisional

meaning: True if the claim clears a named entity or gives a benign explanation for observed activity
used_by_rule: A released exonerating claim needs expiry, retest_date, counterexample_source and cited_versions (manuscript Section 6.5; S4.1)

meaning: Fixed date on which the claim expires once released
used_by_rule: A released exonerating claim cannot pass without it; the release decision keeps it with the released claim (S4.1)

meaning: Date by which the claim is re-tested against independent counterexamples
used_by_rule: A released exonerating claim cannot pass without it (manuscript Section 6.5)

meaning: Source of counterexamples independent of the writer, such as closed cases or reviewers who did not write the claim
used_by_rule: A released exonerating claim cannot pass without it (manuscript Section 6.5)

meaning: Version of each cited record and of any cluster the claim concerns
used_by_rule: A revision of that evidence or a change in that cluster's membership expires the released claim early (S4.1)

meaning: Query runs whose gateway coverage records support an absence claim
used_by_rule: The claim passes only if the cited runs' evaluated entities, sources and intervals together cover the claim's entities, sources and interval, and each part relied on comes from a run whose derived status is complete for that part; a scope-limited run confines the claim to the authorized scope

meaning: Channel-status records for each affected item and outcome channel at the read time: channel state (open, temporarily delayed or not yet opened, permanently closed, reopened or extended by a recorded rule event, or unknown), no-report status (pending, matured or no defined window) with the rule version under which a channel matured, and any recorded decision or rule event that changed the channel's meaning
used_by_rule: An unreported outcome supports a provisional negative only where each cited channel matured with no report under its original meaning; the negative cites the rule version and read time under which the channel matured. A pending, delayed, closed or unknown channel, or one without a defined window, supports no negative; a matured absence on a channel whose meaning a decision or rule event changed supports none for the original outcome (manuscript Section 5.3; S4.1)
